prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage, induction through screening, sorting, make-up to Outbound Load Control Desk handoff; airline loading excluded. Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor, alias Tern (congestion/overload/recovery authorization, priority, make-up release, dispositions beyond operator authority; stops induction if unsafe; uses Chute Occupancy Note; controls holds; ensures holds/exceptions have owners before continuing). Security Duty Manager (alarm decisions, clears security holds, access control; checks Custody Seal Log, escalates discrepancies). Explosives Response Team, alias Pebble (holds/exams, Custody Seal Log, secures area, communicates dispositions). Maintenance Technician (isolates energy, clears jams, consults Recovery Route Card, Calibration Witness Tag, reports faults before return to service). Airline Ramp Coordinator (Carousel Release Slip to Carousel 7). Induction: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit (Oversize Exception Ticket to Image Resolution Desk); Bag Tag Printer (Calibration Witness Tag, replacement tags); Transfer Bag Feeder (Late Transfer Bag Card to Bag Reconciliation Station); Induction Tray Conveyor (meters; only readable, validly routed bags; stop blocks entry). Control: Baggage Control System, alias Velvet (authoritative record of identity, flight, disposition, status; sort plans, cutoffs; receives Flight Cutoff Advisory; diverts to Secondary Inspection Chute; authorizes rejoin). Concourse Zone Controller, alias Mosslight (induction permissive, Recovery Route Card, lanes). Flight Data Gateway, alias Lantern (flight/destination data, Flight Cutoff Advisory). Screening: North Gate Scanner, alias Kestrel, and South Gate Scanner (Manual Rescan Receipt to Image Resolution Desk; results used only if healthy; fault holds feed). Image Resolution Desk records disposition before continuation. Secondary Inspection Chute kept clear. Bag Reconciliation Station (Bag Match Query; mismatch holds). Primary Crossbelt Sorter, alias Juniper (Chute Occupancy Note; routes cleared bags, diverts unresolved). Make-up: East (guards closed, capacity)/West Make-Up Conveyors; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit, alias Orchard (releases only with valid disposition and destination; held if obstructed). Requirements: hold bad-data, unscreened, missed-cutoff, unresolved bags in controlled area; incomplete exams never cleared; safe stop; guards/bypass approved only; custody controlled until loading handoff; restricted access. Recovery: inspect, account for bags, approve route changes, record disposition; restart needs personnel clear, guards

New part:
S218: The Bag Reconciliation Station compares scanned bag identities against the expected flight population and flags missing or duplicate records for resolution.
S219: The Airline Ramp Coordinator uses the Bag Match Query to review unresolved bag-to-flight mismatches before loading authorization is granted.
S220: The East Make-Up Conveyor moves reconciled bags toward the correct flight position without bypassing required identity checks.
S221: The West Make-Up Conveyor remains subject to the same controlled access and reconciliation rules as other make-up equipment.
S222: The Transfer Bag Feeder accepts transfer bags only when their identity and intended onward flight can be verified.
S223: The Outbound Load Control Desk confirms that the flight assignment, reconciled bag count, and operational status are consistent before accepting the loading record.
S224: Before aircraft loading, the Airline Ramp Coordinator verifies that the bag identity is readable, the flight assignment is current, and the security disposition permits loading.
S225: The physical bags presented for loading must agree with the reconciled records, and every unexplained count or identity difference blocks acceptance.
S226: A bag is ready for departure only after screening release, custody continuity, final reconciliation, and loading checks are all complete and recorded.
S227: Operational monitoring provides a continuous view of baggage throughput, equipment availability, queue growth, screening status, and reconciliation exceptions.
S228: The Baggage Control System records bag events and reports missing, duplicate, or delayed event sequences for operational review.
S229: The Concourse Zone Controller reports equipment state changes and alarm conditions to the operations monitoring function.
S230: The Induction Tray Conveyor is monitored for stops, accumulation, and sustained operation below its approved rate.
S231: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter is monitored for availability, recirculation, fault frequency, and output rate against the approved operating plan.
S232: North Gate Scanner performance is assessed using availability, image capture quality, alarm frequency, and screening completion records.
S233: South Gate Scanner performance is assessed using the same approved service measures and screening completion criteria.
S234: The Image Resolution Desk reports unresolved images, review backlog, and processing time against the locally approved service target.
S235: The Bag Reconciliation Station reports unmatched records and count differences, which remain subject to resolution before acceptance.
S236: The Flight Data Gateway is monitored for message timeliness, completeness, and interface errors affecting flight assignment data.
S237: The Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit is monitored for service availability, transaction completion, and accumulation at its entry point.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
